name: Volkswagen VR6 2.8 L 12-valve (AAA, 1991-1999)
summary: Two staggered rows of three cylinders at 15 degrees under one head; even 120-degree firing, but intake and exhaust port lengths differ between the rows, which is the usual explanation for its off-beat growl.

rod_length_mm.note: From a translated Golf Mk3 repair-manual site (not VW's own document).

compression_ratio.note: Wikipedia cites Clemens (Motorbooks) and vwmanual.ru agrees. Wikipedia's engine list gives 10.5:1 for the whole 2.8 12v group, which matches the later AFP engine, not the AAA.

firing_order.note: Also motor-car.net. The same vwmanual.ru page prints 1-3-5-6-2-4 in its ignition section, which looks like a typo. Cylinder numbering and which cylinders are in the front or rear row were NOT found on an opened page.

crank.value: six throws, seven main bearings; connecting-rod journals offset 22 degrees to one another; cylinder centrelines offset 12.5 mm from the crankshaft centreline
crank.note: The 22-degree journal offset is also on Wikipedia (citing Raven & Erickson, Water-Cooled VW Performance Handbook). The 12.5 mm cylinder offset is from motor-car.net only, whose text appears to be an older Wikipedia revision.

firing_intervals_deg.note: 'This also allows the use of a 120 deg firing interval between cylinders.' Even fire.

intake_lift_mm.note: Stock cam data not found. Only aftermarket cam listings surfaced in search.

port_length_asymmetry.value: intake and exhaust port lengths differ between the two cylinder rows; no dimensions published on any opened page
port_length_asymmetry.note: Wikipedia (flagged citation-needed): the differences are compensated by intake manifold runner length, cam overlap and lift profile, or a combination. No dimensions found. Which row has the long intake port was not stated on any opened page.

intake_type.value: single intake manifold feeding both rows, multi-point injection with six manifold-sited injectors (Bosch Motronic)
intake_type.note: Throttle arrangement and plenum details not stated on the page.

missing: cylinder numbering and which cylinders are in which row
intake and exhaust port lengths per row

sources.what: Wikipedia, VR6 engine. Bore, stroke, V angle, CR, valve sizes, 22-degree journal offset, port-length asymmetry (uncited).
vwmanual.ru English translation of a Golf Mk3 repair manual specification page for the AAA. Rod length, firing order, valve head diameters, idle speed. Not a VW document.
motor-car.net VR6 page (text derived from an older Wikipedia revision plus a data table). 120-degree interval, 12.5 mm cylinder offset, firing order.
Wikipedia list of discontinued VW Group petrol engines. Displacement, power, torque.

curb_kg.note: 'Installed in an 2541 lb/1155 kg package'. Launch figure, standard not stated. A reference site (cars-data.com) gives 1207 kg for the five-door; not used.

gear_count.note: German Wikipedia, Golf III: '5-Gang-Schaltgetriebe'; cars-data.com: 'Number of Gears 5'. Cross-check grade; Motor Sport does not state the count.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size 205/50 R15 (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio): unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius.

tyre.note: '205/50 rubber in place of the GTI's comparatively modest 195/50. Both Golfs utilise 15 in wheel diameters, but with 6 and 6.5J as standard issue, respectively.'

top_speed_kmh.note: 'the 140 mph hatchback has arrived'; Motor Sport, October 1992: 'attaining a maximum of 123 and 140 mph respectively' (GTI, VR6). Converted by me (225.3 km/h). German Wikipedia and cars-data.com give 224 km/h.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Volkswagen Golf Mk3' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front engine, front-wheel drive / Syncro four-wheel drive. The VR6 is taken as front-wheel drive (the Syncro was a separate version), our reading.

sources.what: Motor Sport magazine, October 1991, 'New cars: Volkswagen Golf': launch report on the Golf III VR6 (174 bhp): claimed weight and top speed.
Motor Sport magazine, October 1992, 'Sensible and seductive': UK test of the Golf GTI and VR6: tyres and wheels, maximum speed.
